proposals.entity_key: Immediate past in imparfait (venir de + infinitive)

evidence.notes: Formation is explicit; venir carries the imparfait marking and de links it to the infinitive.
The imparfait is a simple tense, so the verb slot is filled by one word with no auxiliary or participle; the rule gives no explicit formation string.

proposals.value: subject + imparfait + habitual time expression (souvent, tous les jours, le mardi)

evidence.notes: Habitual markers such as souvent, chaque jour, le vendredi accompany the imparfait; English used to / would map onto this pattern.

proposals.value: imparfait clause + quand/soudain + passé composé clause

evidence.notes: Formation is explicit; the continuous background action stays in the imparfait and the interrupting event follows in the passé composé, optionally with depuis + duration.
Formation is stated verbatim; être is the exception with the stem ét-.

proposals.value: spelling change (e or ç) kept before -ais, -ais, -ait, -aient but not before -ions, -iez

evidence.notes: The extra e of manger and ç of commencer appear only in the je/tu/il/ils persons; the nous and vous forms drop them.

proposals.entity_key: Imparfait vs passé composé with state verbs
proposals.value: subject + imparfait for states; subject + auxiliary (avoir/être) + past participle for changes

evidence.notes: State verbs (être, avoir, penser, croire, savoir, espérer, sembler, paraître) take the simple imparfait form for states but the compound auxiliary + participle form when a change or specific realization is meant.
Formation is explicit and vouloir has only this vous imperative form; no tu or nous imperative exists.

proposals.entity_key: Impersonal expressions followed by the indicative

evidence.notes: Formation 'Impersonal expression + que + indicative'; the listed expressions (il est certain, il est sûr, il est évident, il est vrai, il est probable, il me semble) express certainty or probability.

proposals.entity_key: Impersonal expressions followed by the subjunctive

evidence.notes: Formation 'Impersonal expression + que + subjunctive'; the que clause verb is subjunctive after expressions of necessity, possibility, emotion or doubt.
